thread:
yuko: bringing up tahiti-v1 int8 on staging. noticed BLEU dip vs fp16 on a small JP+AR+emoji eval. looks tied to ZWJ/emoji anchors and RTL embedding offsets. anyone around?
mateo: can you paste a minimal failing sample and which quant mode? int8 straight or mixed q5 fallback?
yuko: int8 straight from onboarding. sample: '今日はエモジ😊 السلام‍' -> host detok vs runtime detok:
```
host_detok: 今日は エモジ😊 السلام‍
host_tokens: ['今日は',' ','エモジ','😊',' ','السلام‍']
runtime_detok: 今日は エモジ😊السلام‍
runtime_tokens: ['今日は',' ','エモジ😊السلام‍']
```
yuko: runtime glued emoji+arabic word into one token occasionally, and decoder then flips bracket/anchor orientation when rendering RTL segments. BLEU on our mixed-orient shortctx set dropped 1.7 points on int8.
dina: interesting. are you running sampling? kv_cache? any kernel fallbacks?
yuko: sampling off for the BLEU run (greedy), kv_cache enabled, batch=4 to surface batching effects. no fallback. ran tokenizer_parity on 2k mixed samples -> mismatch ~0.09%, concentrated on sequences with ZWJ or emoji followed by RTL chars.
mateo: 0.09% focused on emoji/ZWJ is consistent with a pretokenizer or gap-handling difference. two quick checks: 1) run with `--no-kv-cache` to see if batching/kvcache causes boundary coalescing 2) run with `--norm NFKC` vs NFC to see if emoji/ZWJ normalization differs.
yuko: ran A/B: no-kv-cache -> tokens match host and BLEU matches fp16. switching to NFKC didn't change. suspect kv_cache + batch-induced key aliasing because emoji+succeeding script cause different key lengths after quant rounding.
dina: can you collect per-batch kvcache entry lengths and a hex-hash for keys: `TRACE=kv KVCACHE_DEBUG=1 python run_onboard.py --quantize int8 --batch 4 --input-file evals/mixed-orient/shortctx-200.jsonl`
yuko: kicked off trace run (run id 3210007788). trace-bot: attached artifacts -> https://internal.storage/runs/3210007788.
mateo: if we see kv keys with identical truncated prefixes, int8 quant rounding on qkv kernels could be collapsing small differences. propose bisect: int8 -> q5 -> fp16, and also try building with `KVCACHE_STRICT=true` which uses full-width keys (perf hit) to confirm. I can start bisect.
yuko: please start bisect. i'll upload a tiny notebook that diffs detok and kvcache key histograms. also adding a short eval (200 samples) that includes emoji+ZWJ+RTL anchors to onboard tests.
dina: follow-ups: mateo -> bisect + KVCACHE_STRICT test, yuko -> trace notebook + eval set, ci-bot -> create an onboard CI job suggestion: run 40 mixed-orient samples with batch=4 kv_cache on and assert tokenizer parity >= 99.85% for greedy. ci-bot: created issue #ML-5592 for CI job.
yuko: thanks all. will ping once bisect completes. :eyes:
